transcript.text: Bosch built-in microwave BFL524MS0B randomly stops part way through cooking, time still on the display. Opening and closing the door lets it carry on. Maybe once every few days.

This behaviour—where the microwave stops but the clock stays on, and restarting (by opening/closing the door) fixes it—is classic for a faulty door interlock system. The microwave thinks the door has opened because one of the safety switches inside the latch is failing to stay engaged. Since this happens intermittently, it could be a worn switch or a slight misalignment in the latch mechanism. Please do not try to open the casing yourself as there are high-voltage components inside that can hold a charge even when unplugged. For now, please check:
1. Is the door release button loose, floppy, or unusually stiff compared to usual?
2. Look at the plastic hooks on the edge of the door and the slots they click into—are there any cracks or signs of wear? If the button feels loose or a hook is broken, that suggests the mechanical cause. If it looks fine, the internal switch itself is likely failing and will need replacement by an engineer.

I can't tell whether the release button feels loose or stiff compared to before. There was some grease around the door hooks and latch slots, which I cleaned off, but it still happened once since. The door might sit very slightly lower on the handle side, though I can't be sure. No burning smell, sparks or tripping, and I'm not taking it out of the housing.

Since cleaning the grease didn't resolve it and you can't be sure about the button feel, this points to an internal issue: either the plastic latch is worn slightly out of shape (your note about the door sitting lower supports this), or one of the internal safety switches that tells the microwave 'the door is shut' is failing. Because opening and closing the door resets it, the appliance isn't detecting a continuous closed state. As this is a built-in Bosch model, you should contact Bosch support immediately; it is likely still under warranty and they can arrange for an engineer to replace the faulty interlock switch or latch assembly safely.
